markdown_report:
At 10% progress, retain **specificity-gated repeated-support lexical fusion** as a controlled hypothesis, with reduced novelty claims and stronger attenuation controls. Its benefit remains untested.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Repeated support offers an identifiable historical connection. Distinct IDs prevent self-voting, but product variants can inflate support. (2) Recency attenuates older evidence. It cannot establish satisfied demand or current intent. (3) Fixed features aid attribution. The supplied historical score, 0.5587, supports retaining that comparator, not attributing its performance to specificity.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) motivates objective controls. Its gains do not identify the winning loss here. (2) [Recurrence-filtered TF–IDF](https://www.sciencedirect.com/org/science/article/pii/S2334454722000235) closely anticipates the gate. Recurrence and temporal weighting therefore offer limited ingredient novelty. (3) [Fusion analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11934) motivates scale controls. Masking may help simply by reducing interference.

The framework separates three directions: objective discrimination, lexical evidence selection, and directional prediction. Evidence selection further separates corpus frequency, within-history recurrence, recency, and residual magnitude; these require separate controls.

| Idea | O/P/U/M/D scores | Assessment: positive; negative |
|---|---|---|
| Matched multi-negative objective comparison | 2/7/3/8/3 | O: controlled application; established. P: reusable; gains unknown. U: improves discrimination; lacks explicit intent mechanism. M: targets pair errors; calibration unproven. D: localized; exposure matching needs care. |
| Specificity-gated lexical residual | 2/6/7/6/6 | O: testable integration; close prior art. P: inspectable; vocabulary brittle. U: targets broad and stale evidence; usefulness unverified. M: combined-score supervision; generalization unknown. D: fixed features; causal scoring and controls substantial. |
| Recent-source directed-transition residual | 4/7/6/6/6 | O: useful synthesis; established components. P: follow-on associations; sparse edges. U: recent links; compatibility unknown. M: ranking signal; popularity confounding. D: sparse counts; leakage control required. |

Scores denote originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment, and difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

**Chosen algorithm.** Retain the recency-weighted, distinct-item TF–IDF pool. Mask profile dimensions unless their tokens satisfy frozen training-corpus frequency limits and occur in at least two distinct recent items. Candidate overlap then contributes through the masked dot product; this is a profile-feature mask, not a separate candidate gate. Do not renormalize after masking. Keep confidence outside normalization and initialize amplitude at zero.

This targets broad associations and stale or isolated evidence. Combined-score multi-negative training targets Electronics’ supplied 16.98% sampled-pair error rate; improvement remains hypothetical.

Compare objective-only, unchanged residual, and gated residual. Include zero amplitude, equally retuned unmasked fusion, and frequency-matched random-mask diagnostics. Separate specificity from attenuation and audit duplicate overlap. Preserve seeds, routes, adapters, predictor parity, and budget. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10; retain the incumbent on ties. [Sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) do not establish full-catalog superiority, and [adaptive selection](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) limits post-selection uncertainty claims.

idea.description: Evaluate a recurrence-and-corpus-frequency mask on the fixed lexical profile added to per-dataset SASRec. Tokens must occur in at least two distinct recent historical item IDs and pass frozen training-corpus document-frequency limits. Candidates receive a residual through overlap with this masked profile. This is an incremental, untested integration with close content-profile prior art; its principal research question is whether evidence selection helps beyond merely attenuating the residual.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations, stale historical demand, and recommendations without an identifiable connection. Recent, repeated token evidence provides an inspectable historical link and attenuates isolated or older evidence, although lexical specificity is only a proxy for relevance. Combined-score multi-negative training addresses weak sampled training-pair separation, particularly Electronics. Neither recurrence nor recency establishes current need, satisfied demand, compatibility, or useful complementarity. Training margins do not establish validation gains.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an implementation specification; no execution, successful parity check, or new performance result is claimed. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, unchanged splits and routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS with effective default 200. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions, and observed timestamps. Generic metadata examples do not authorize review ratings/text or item ratings/categories/prices/stores. Do not fetch pretrained weights or additional datasets, inspect hidden test files, or change the evaluator.

Comparator and text reproducibility: prefer complete, compatible incumbent artifacts, including preprocessing and pooling configuration; a historical scalar score alone is insufficient. Preserve its tokenizer, vocabulary scope, support rule, optimizer, and checkpoint schedule for the matched comparison. If those artifacts are unavailable, explicitly declare a fresh comparator rather than claiming exact reproduction of 0.5587. For that fresh comparator, use sklearn TfidfVectorizer with lowercase=True, strip_accents=None, analyzer='word', token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b', ngram_range=(1,1), min_df=2, max_df=0.95, max_features=50000, sublinear_tf=True, norm='l2', dtype=float32, and no stop-word list. Concatenate title, one space, and description, joining description lists in their supplied order; absent fields become empty strings. Record library versions and persist the fitted vocabulary and IDF rather than relying on refitting. Treat HTML cleaning as a separate diagnostic intervention, not an undeclared preprocessing change.

Fit vocabulary and document frequencies on distinct items appearing in training histories only. N is that distinct training-item count, including empty-text documents. Transform other permitted catalog metadata with the frozen vocabulary; missing or entirely out-of-vocabulary text yields a zero row. Padding always has a zero row. Freeze eligible tokens using 2 <= df <= floor(0.05*N). If this produces no eligible dimensions, report zero activation rather than changing thresholds after validation. The 5% threshold is a declared hypothesis. Corpus rarity and within-user recurrence are separate mechanisms; neither proves semantic specificity. Metadata snapshots are not guaranteed to reflect historical availability, so make no timestamp-level text-availability claim.

Exact fresh-comparator pooling: at every supervised position use only its causal sequence prefix, including the current input item and excluding future events and the shifted target event. Never remove earlier events because their ID equals the target. Take the last 20 nonpadding events, retain the latest occurrence of each distinct ID, and retain its actual event age within the original window. Let x_j be the fixed normalized TF–IDF row. For m distinct IDs, a_j is the mean nonnegative cosine with the other m-1 rows; use zero when m<2. Let r_j=2^(-age_j/5), w_j=r_j*a_j, S=sum(w), and p=normalize_or_zero(sum_j w_j*x_j). Set c=S/(S+1), returning p=0,c=0 when the pool norm is zero. Missing-text rows contribute zero similarities. An existing compatible incumbent rule can replace this rule only if it is documented and shared across both residual conditions.

Gate and scoring: count each token once per distinct window item, using nonzero TF–IDF entries. Let b_t be one when token t is corpus-eligible and appears in at least two distinct retained IDs. Define z=p elementwise-multiplied by b and do not renormalize z. Score s_i=h dot e_i + alpha*c*(z dot x_i). The unmasked comparator substitutes p for z, keeping all other operations identical. This is a history-profile mask: candidate dependence comes from the dot product with x_i. With nonnegative normalized TF–IDF, 0<=z dot x_i<=1, but masking changes magnitude and relative candidate preferences simultaneously. Confidence is applied after normalization so it cannot cancel. Initialize alpha directly at zero, exclude it from weight decay, and project it into [0,A] after each optimizer step. The direct parameter has a nonzero score derivative at zero; clamp-induced boundary behavior should be logged. Primary A=1 is scale-sensitive, not a validated optimum. At zero amplitude, the fixed text pipeline requires no gradients.

Objective: use positive-plus-32-negative sampled cross-entropy, temperature 1, averaging over eligible nonpadding positions. Draw uniform negatives without replacement using a dedicated seed-42 generator, excluding padding, the target, and causal-prefix IDs only. If fewer than 32 eligible items exist, use all of them and mask unused slots; omit positions with none. Record sampling order and duplicate handling. This is a sampled ranking surrogate without LogQ correction, not an unbiased full-softmax estimator. Prefix filtering does not eliminate latent false negatives. Share or deterministically regenerate identical negative streams across conditions. Match initialization, backbone, optimizer, learning rate, regularization, loader order, sequence length, checkpoint schedule, and completed training exposure for attribution; record all resolved baseline settings. GPU cost must also be reported because matched exposure need not mean equal cost. Do not silently substitute time-limited unequal-exposure comparisons for mechanistic controls.

Primary comparisons and scale controls: compare objective-only, unmasked residual, and gated residual under the same objective. Include alpha=0 explicitly. Predeclare cap candidates A in {0,1,2} for both residual families, admitting only complete, equally budgeted comparisons that fit the remaining allowance; if this family is unaffordable, retain A=1 and qualify scale attribution as unresolved. Count every additional trained configuration as a charged trial. Matched retuning is needed because an unmasked comparator with an unsuitable amplitude can exaggerate masking gains. Small validation improvements do not justify claiming a specificity mechanism.

Low-cost diagnostic framework: on the same frozen compatible checkpoint, compare last-item cosine, normalized history centroid, exponential-recency centroid, recurrence-only centroid, and the selected profile. Separately remove the corpus-frequency filter and the recurrence filter. These are inference interventions, not equally trained competitors. For scale analysis, use deterministic training-visible fixtures and a common candidate list per prefix to center each residual over candidates and calculate its RMS. Where both RMS values exceed 1e-8, rescale masked residuals to the unmasked RMS; report zero-RMS cases separately without division or arbitrary replacement. This fixture-only intervention isolates some magnitude effects but changes the deployed rule and does not establish retrained validation superiority.

Random-mask control: for each prefix, partition nonzero profile dimensions by floor(log2(max(df,1))). In each bin, randomly retain the same number of dimensions retained by the proposed gate, using a separate analysis generator seeded 42 and a fixed fixture order. This matches retained feature count and coarse document-frequency distribution, not exact removed mass or semantics. Use ten predeclared random realizations if the diagnostic reserve permits; otherwise declare the smaller count before execution. Compare removed norm, centered candidate residual RMS, support activation, and rank changes. Do not select a favorable realization. These controls and RMS matching are diagnostic unless separately trained and charged.

Shortcut and duplication audits: compute exact groups from complete lowercase whitespace-normalized titles and descriptions, excluding empty strings. For a predeclared near-duplicate diagnostic, use training-fitted character 3-5-gram TF–IDF and cosine >=0.95, comparing only the bounded history-target pairs in the diagnostic fixtures to avoid catalog-wide similarity matrices. Record the tokenizer, vectorizer settings, scope, and threshold; this defines lexical similarity, not verified product families. Compare title-only, description-only, HTML/CSS-cleaned text, and an alphanumeric identifier mask removing tokens containing both letters and digits, together with frequency-matched random masks. Infer any brand-like strings only from supplied text and label them uncertain. Apply interventions consistently to history and candidate rows, rebuild normalization, and report resulting scale changes. Run only predeclared audits that fit the reserve. Rare identifiers may be genuinely useful evidence; masking sensitivity alone does not establish shortcut learning. Report diagnostic outcomes for pairs with and without near-duplicate history-target overlap. Use validation strata only if authorized existing per-user outcomes and item identities are available; otherwise restrict this analysis to training fixtures. Never alter splits or candidates.

Efficient computation: store normalized item rows as float32 CSR. Compute only bounded within-window similarities, sparse profile sums, and sampled-candidate intersections; never construct a catalog-by-catalog matrix. Cache deterministic causal context features when sequence construction and storage permit. Account for CPU preprocessing, device transfers, GPU-active work, and memory. For the twenty native simulator users, five per category, perform blockwise full-catalog scoring, exclude historical IDs, and maintain running top-k with deterministic tie handling. Preserve the evaluator's supplied candidate order and masking behavior for pinned scoring; do not introduce additional seen-item filtering there.

Diagnostics and adapter: preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, with batches (None,sequence,positive,negative), tensors B x L. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module and view.item_emb its collaborative embedding. Preserve user_train, meta_data, and review_data without fabricating unavailable fields. Have log2feats expose collaborative features plus causal context through an explicitly documented packed representation, such as float64 collaborative features followed by the ordered last-20 context IDs, verifying exact integer representation and casting collaborative features back to their scoring dtype inside predict_score. Recompute the identical deduplication, ages, pooling, and gate there. Define separate handling for position-aligned IDs, shared candidate vectors, and per-position candidate matrices; avoid ambiguous broadcasting. Keep embedding-only probes separate from packed features. If another representation is required by the existing adapter, document and update its consumer consistently. Probes must use eval/no_grad, restore prior model mode, and score the deployed residual. Retain finite-score checks, margins, and pair-error rates, with unavailable item-category breakdowns explicitly marked. Embedding cosine remains descriptive rather than proof of collapse or diversity. Add precisely defined support/gate activation, removed squared profile norm, distinct supporting IDs, duplicate concentration, residual RMS, alpha boundary frequency, residual-to-collaborative scale, and candidate rank-change summaries.

Export and parity: update the predictor writer, not only a generated file. Serialize category weights, architecture configuration, mappings, routes, tokenizer settings, vocabulary, document frequencies, IDF, sparse catalog rows, token eligibility, pooling settings, alpha and cap, padding, and truncation. Verify scorer and generated working/predict.py parity on deterministic training-visible fixtures covering empty histories, missing text, repeated IDs, one distinct item, two-item support, ubiquitous words, zero eligible vocabulary, near-identical titles, and mixed-category routes. Verify candidate order, input shapes, finite values, causal-prefix invariance, and full-catalog masking separately. Use torch.testing.assert_close with rtol=1e-5 and atol=1e-6 for float32 scoring, recording discrepancies and any justified tolerance change. Future-event perturbations must leave earlier scores unchanged. Artifact serialization and routing are part of correctness.

Budget, selection, and uncertainty: subtract all previous charged training, diagnostics, debugging, and failures from 43,200 GPU-seconds. Reserve one-sixth of the actual remainder for diagnostics, export, parity checks, and failures; admit the primary three-condition family before optional cap sweeps or extra training. Divide the primary training allocation equally across its twelve category-condition cells and record completed epochs, updates, positions, and cost. A configuration requires valid results for all four categories. If matching exposure cannot fit, report the comparison as budget-efficiency evidence with unequal-exposure limitations. Retain the environment's default 200-epoch ceiling and the recorded baseline checkpoint schedule. Predeclare trial order, validation query schedule, stopping rules, tie handling, and any optional family before observing its results; a report does not reset the shared budget.

Select solely using pinned validation with 200 users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42, and the equally weighted four-category HR@10. Retain the incumbent on exact ties. Report all category scores, macro score, trial count, queries, and cumulative GPU cost. One changed hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Where authorized per-user hit indicators already exist, compute 10,000 paired, within-category bootstrap replicates using analysis seed 42, averaging category differences equally and reporting the percentile 95% interval. Otherwise report this analysis unavailable. The interval conditions on trained models and fixed candidates; it excludes training-seed and candidate variability and does not correct adaptive selection bias. Fixed-seed reruns assess reproducibility, not seed robustness. Treat selected gains as exploratory, freeze the configuration before the independent host test, and never access hidden test labels. Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog superiority; simulator recommendations assess a different setting.

User-facing limitations: track broad-match, stale-interest, uncertain-content, unsupported-task, duplicated-capability, and useful-complement judgments only when the simulator actually supplies them. Do not invent compatibility, ownership, unmet needs, quantities, or diversity/conformity traits. The gate can suppress synonyms, newly emerging interests, sparse histories, and useful complements while still rewarding product variants. Event-age decay does not model elapsed-time seasonality. The supplied 0.5587 and 0.5538 scores are historical observations, not new measurements, compatible-run guarantees, uncertainty estimates, or evidence identifying a mechanism. Learned text encoders and directed transitions remain follow-ups; recurrence-filtered TF–IDF is the appropriate low-complexity next experiment only if the matched controls remain affordable.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIG: preserve four baseline routes; preprocessing_seed=0; training_seed=42
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
CONFIG: window=20; event_half_life=5; confidence_shrinkage=1
CONFIG: negatives=32; temperature=1; primary_alpha_cap=1
CONFIG: effective_epochs=int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))

# Freeze trial list, checkpoint schedule, query rules, and budget before results.
remaining = 43200 - all_previously_charged_GPU_seconds
reserve = remaining / 6
admit_only_complete_comparisons_that_fit(remaining - reserve)

for category in baseline_categories:
    X, vocabulary, df, N = load_compatible_artifacts_or_fit_declared_training_only_TFIDF()
    eligible = (df >= 2) & (df <= floor(0.05*N))

    for condition in ['objective_only', 'unmasked', 'gated']:
        initialize_identical_SASRec(seed=42)
        negative_rng = dedicated_generator(seed=42)
        alpha = trainable_scalar(0.0)

        for batch in unchanged_training_loader:
            h = causal_SASRec_features(batch.sequence)
            losses = []
            for valid position t:
                prefix = batch.sequence through t
                candidates, candidate_mask = positive_plus_uniform_negatives(
                    target=batch.positive[t], count=32, replacement=False,
                    exclude=padding_and_target_and_prefix_ids, rng=negative_rng)
                if no_eligible_negative: continue
                logits = dot(h[t], item_emb(candidates))

                if condition != 'objective_only':
                    events = last_20_nonpadding_events(prefix)
                    ids, ages = latest_occurrence_dedup_with_original_event_ages(events)
                    V = X[ids]
                    agreement[j] = mean_nonnegative_cosine_to_other_distinct_rows(V,j)
                    # Empty comparison sets return zero.
                    w = 2**(-ages/5) * agreement
                    p = normalize_or_zero(sparse_weighted_sum(V,w))
                    c = sum(w)/(sum(w)+1) if norm(p)>0 else 0
                    if condition == 'gated':
                        count = count_nonzero_rows_per_token(V)
                        z = p * (eligible & (count >= 2))
                    else:
                        z = p
                    # Never renormalize z; never use target to construct p or z.
                    logits += alpha*c*sparse_dot(z, X[candidates])

                losses.append(masked_CE(logits, positive_index=0, temperature=1))
            if losses:
                optimize(mean(losses))
                project_alpha_to_interval(0, declared_cap)
            honor_predeclared_checkpoint_schedule_exposure_and_budget()

        export_trial_local_artifacts_and_matching_predictor_writer()
        verify_causal_score_order_shape_and_routing_parity()
        run_adapted_DiagnosisProbe_on_actual_model_with_deployed_scores()

# Optional matched cap family: A in {0,1,2}, equally available to both residuals.
# Every trained configuration and validation query is charged and recorded.
# Frozen diagnostic interventions: centroids, last-item, recurrence/corpus-filter ablations,
# frequency-matched random masks, centered-RMS matching, text-source/identifier masks,
# and duplicate-overlap strata. These are not retrained competitors.
# Bootstrap only authorized existing paired user outcomes; disclose selection bias.
# Select complete configurations by pinned macro validation HR@10; incumbent wins ties.
# Freeze selection before host test; never inspect hidden test labels.

originality.positive: The integration with causal SASRec scoring and explicit attenuation controls provides a useful, independently testable experimental contribution.
originality.negative: Recurrence across at least two history documents has close published precedent; TF–IDF filtering, recency weighting, and additive fusion are established. A score of 4 overstated ingredient novelty.

future_potential.positive: An inspectable baseline can clarify when repeated lexical evidence helps and establish controls for later learned or directional models.
future_potential.negative: Exact-token recurrence is brittle for sparse and emerging interests, can favor duplicates, and cannot establish compatibility or current unmet demand. Broader impact depends on evidence beyond a small sampled validation gain.

code_difficulty.positive: Fixed sparse features and one amplitude preserve the SASRec backbone and avoid another learned encoder.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal sparse computation, exposure-matched controls, magnitude diagnostics, feature transport, full-catalog scoring, and reproducible predictor serialization make the complete study more demanding than the small scoring equation suggests.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequence encoder and item-scoring baseline.
limitations: Does not supply the proposed explicit lexical evidence mask or establish current unmet needs.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates examining generalized BCE and negative-sampling effects before adding model capacity.
limitations: Reported gains do not establish improvement under this Amazon protocol.
Calibration and negative count require separate controls; positive BCE reweighting is not equivalent to the documented gBCE transformation.

related_work.title: Turning Dross Into Gold Loss
contributions: Supplies a practical multi-negative cross-entropy direction for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Objective changes alone do not explicitly distinguish specific current interests from broad or stale associations.

related_work.title: LSIDN
contributions: Motivates separating persistent interests from recent behavior.
limitations: Does not establish identifiable intent or validate the proposed lexical mask on these four datasets.

related_work.title: DTR4Rec
contributions: Motivates directed transition and short-window association signals as an alternative research direction.
limitations: Predictive transitions do not establish compatibility, complementarity, or unmet demand.

related_work.title: 2022 content-recommendation study using recurring TF–IDF terms
contributions: The supplied search describes averaging TF–IDF scores for terms appearing in at least two historical documents, providing close prior art for recurrence filtering.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this SASRec integration or the pinned Amazon evaluation.
The supplied excerpt does not establish equivalence of the full scoring and temporal-weighting procedures.

related_work.title: Temporal user-profile study
contributions: Provides precedent for temporal user profiles and decay weighting.
limitations: Temporal weighting does not establish satisfied demand, current intent, or transfer to this benchmark.

related_work.title: TfidfVectorizer documentation
contributions: Defines reproducible corpus-frequency filtering, tokenization, and TF–IDF settings.
limitations: Corpus document-frequency thresholds differ from recurrence within an individual user's history.

related_work.title: Analysis of fusion in hybrid retrieval
contributions: Motivates examining fusion weights, normalization, and residual scale.
limitations: Does not show that masking improves semantic specificity or recommendation quality in this task.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog model orderings.
limitations: Metric corrections cannot replace the mandated evaluator.
Its findings qualify interpretation rather than invalidate selection under the pinned candidate protocol.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides paired-bootstrap precedent adapted here to within-category user resampling.
limitations: This adaptation does not capture training-seed variation, candidate variation, or adaptive model-selection bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit validation feedback.
limitations: Ordinary post-selection bootstrap intervals do not remove this bias.

related_work.title: The reusable holdout
contributions: Motivates caution about repeated adaptive validation queries.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the mandated splits or implementing a different host evaluation protocol.

related_work.title: Amazon review data documentation
contributions: Documents plausible catalog redundancy and metadata markup issues that motivate text audits.
limitations: Does not establish duplicate prevalence or text artifacts in this pinned dataset.
Does not authorize accessing unavailable reviews or metadata fields.

related_work.title: Supplied shortcut-learning benchmark
contributions: Motivates testing lexical correlations with targeted and frequency-matched random interventions.
limitations: Does not establish that rare identifiers are shortcuts in this recommendation benchmark.

related_work.title: Content-Based Top-N Recommendation using Heterogeneous Relations
contributions: Provides precedent for learned global term weighting as a future content comparator.
limitations: Requires a separately controlled implementation and does not establish gains here.

related_work.title: Ask the GRU
contributions: Motivates comparing mean-pooled word embeddings with recurrent text encoders if learned text representations are later introduced.
limitations: Its use of pretrained embeddings and optional tag supervision limits transfer to this no-pretrained-weights setting.
Description word order and chronological interaction order require separate ablations.
